tools_used: provisioned snapshot and documents (petition, BIO, QP, both merits briefs)
CourtListener MCP search + read_document (Eighth Circuit opinion)
WebFetch of the public supremecourt.gov docket and the two SG briefs
two subagents to summarize the merits briefs
helpful: Provisioned merits briefs for both sides were the single most useful input; documents.json made their provenance clear.
The statpack merits table with its excluded column gave a quotable, guard-checked baseline.
CourtListener read_document returned the Eighth Circuit opinion cleanly in one call.
gaps: The SG's CVSG brief and merits-stage amicus briefs are not provisioned even though the docket records them; the CVSG brief especially is a standard predictor input and had to be fetched and text-extracted by hand (WebFetch could not read the PDF; pypdf did).

fedcourts query has no topic/text filter on SCOTUS rows, so it cannot surface doctrinally similar merits priors (takings, federal-vs-state-law) — the two queries run contributed nothing to the forecast.
No per-Term merits lineup data (SG-as-amicus win rate, affirmance rate in one-vs-many splits) is published in the pack; those adjustments came from general knowledge.
notes: Grant Term read from event opened_at-adjacent docket text (Petition GRANTED 2026-06-29) as OT2025; pooled merits baseline computed over the rendered 2017-2024 rows since the table omits Terms with no parsed judgment.
